notes:
Account background: Brookside Helix is a mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) with a heavy focus on in-app search, insights, and anomaly detection. Product org wants semantic search to power: 1) in-app help and docs search, 2) analyst-facing insights explorer, 3) nightly batch re-embedding of event metadata for feature experiments.

Engagement summary: initial interest in Hosted API for fast proof-of-concept: quick quality checks on embeddings and reranking. After hosted trial, they plan a Dedicated evaluation for predictable throughput and unit-cost reduction for large nightly jobs. Cost sensitivity moderate — will trade latency for lower cost where feasible.

Technical requirements / highlights:
- Workloads: online semantic search queries (peak 200–400 qps during business hours), user-facing top-k recall and reranking; nightly batch: ~100k–250k rows/day to embed and upsert into vector DB.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile retrieval + rerank under 150ms (aim <100ms for primary flows). Embedding generation latency for single-item requests <60ms preferred for interactive flows; batch throughput must support overnight windows.
- Vector DB: primary preference is Pinecone or Weaviate for hosted POC; long-term open to self-hosted Milvus on Dedicated. Must support metric (cosine/inner) and efficient upserts.
- Data flow: source = Postgres + S3; metadata stored in Postgres, vectors in vector DB. They want Redwood to provide clear batching and retry guidance for ETL jobs and a recommended batching config.
- Model preferences: start with mid-size open models (cost/quality tradeoff), evaluate quantized Open RMs for Dedicated. Need ability to route to smaller, cheaper variants for non-critical re-ranks.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML) mandatory; audit logging and KMS integration required; primary data residency in EU (Ireland) for EU customers.

POC plan agreed (high-level):
- Phase 1 (hosted API, 2 weeks): run embedding quality tests on sample corpus (50k rows), validate Pinecone integration, collect latency & cost metrics.
- Phase 2 (hosted load soak, 1 week): simulate peak query mix (~400 qps) to surface tail latency and cold-start issues.
- Phase 3 (dedicated POC, 3–4 weeks): provision small dedicated pool (N GPUs), run full nightly batch (100k–250k), measure unit cost and end-to-end SLA.

Customer quotes / misc:
- "If we can get consistent recall and cut nightly costs by 40% vs. Hosted, Dedicated is a go." — Head of Product
- Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization profiles.
